sec: Ominous octet and pathophysiology of T2DM

items.q: Match the following organ to its role in the ominous octet — 1) Liver 2) Pancreas (β-cell) 3) Skeletal muscle 4) Adipocyte … A) Increased gluconeogenesis B) Decreased insulin secretion C) Impaired GLUT4 translocation D) Increased lipolysis
items.exp: The octet identifies liver (↑ gluconeogenesis), pancreas (↓ secretion), muscle (impaired GLUT4) and fat (↑ lipolysis) as four of the eight defects. (Book p918)

items.q: A T2DM patient has fasting hyperglycaemia despite normal insulin sensitivity on clamp. Which octet member is most directly implicated?
opts: Increased hepatic gluconeogenesis (most important per source)
items.exp: The page marks increased hepatic gluconeogenesis as the most important driver of fasting hyperglycaemia in T2DM. (Book p918)

items.q: Assess the octet: I β-cell dysfunction in T2DM is reversible with early therapy. II Skeletal muscle insulin resistance precedes β-cell failure.
items.exp: β-cell dysfunction in T2DM is largely irreversible once established; muscle insulin resistance typically precedes β-cell exhaustion. (Book p918)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a tissue where insulin normally increases glucose uptake via GLUT4?
items.exp: Liver uses GLUT2 (insulin-independent), whereas skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and adipose tissue depend on insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation. (Book p918)

items.q: Per the page, the single most important contributor to fasting hyperglycaemia in T2DM is increased ___.
items.exp: Increased hepatic gluconeogenesis is the most important driver of fasting hyperglycaemia in T2DM on this page. (Book p918)

items.q: Match the following organ to its insulin-resistance effect — 1) Liver 2) Muscle 3) Adipocyte 4) Brain … A) ↑Gluconeogenesis B) ↓GLUT4-mediated uptake C) ↑Lipolysis / FFA flux D) Insulin-independent GLUT1 uptake
items.exp: Insulin resistance in liver drives gluconeogenesis; in muscle impairs GLUT4; in adipose tissue increases lipolysis with FFA flux; brain glucose uptake is insulin-independent via GLUT1. (Book p918)

items.q: An obese T2DM patient has high portal free-fatty-acid flux. The downstream effect on the liver is most consistent with:
items.exp: Portal FFA flux drives hepatic gluconeogenesis and steatosis; it does not decrease VLDL output. (Book p918)

items.q: Assess this caveat: I CPT-1 is physiologically absent in liver; fatty-acyl-CoA accumulation in the schematic leads to insulin resistance. II Insulin normally suppresses hormone-sensitive lipase in adipocytes.
items.exp: The schematic depicts CPT-1 as 'Absent in liver' which is biologically inaccurate; insulin normally suppresses HSL in adipocytes. (Book p918)

items.q: Match the following defect to the source's description — 1) β-cell 2) α-cell 3) Incretin axis 4) Kidney … A) Decreased insulin secretion B) Hyperglucagonaemia C) Reduced GLP-1 effect D) Increased glucose reabsorption (SGLT2)
items.exp: β-cell defect is decreased insulin secretion; α-cell shows hyperglucagonaemia; incretin axis is reduced GLP-1 effect; the kidney shows increased SGLT2-mediated glucose reabsorption. (Book p918)

items.q: Which drug class targets the kidney component of the ominous octet?
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce renal glucose reabsorption; sulfonylureas target the β-cell; TZDs target adipose tissue; α-glucosidase inhibitors target intestinal carbohydrate absorption. (Book p918)

items.q: Which organ provides the dominant source of fasting endogenous glucose in T2DM?
items.exp: Hepatic gluconeogenesis dominates fasting glucose production in T2DM. (Book p918)

items.q: The 'ominous octet' highlights defects in pancreas, liver, muscle, fat, brain, gut (incretin), kidney and ___.
items.exp: α-cell hyperglucagonaemia is the eighth member; the others include incretin deficiency, SGLT2 upregulation and CNS dysregulation. (Book p918)

items.q: Assess incretin physiology: I GLP-1 and GIP are secreted by intestinal cells. II The incretin effect is preserved in T2DM.
items.exp: GLP-1 (L-cells) and GIP (K-cells) are secreted by the gut; the incretin effect is reduced in T2DM, prompting GLP-1 agonist therapy. (Book p918)
